classification.difficultyReason: Link normalisation, branch integration and symmetry, then accumulate the second CDF branch from F(0)=1/2; the requested intervals scaffold these routine procedures.

content.prompt:
A probability density function is defined piecewise by
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}k(4+x)&-4\le x\le0,\\k(4-x)&0\le x\le4.\end{cases}$$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the value of the constant $k$. Hence write the equation of $f(x)$ and sketch it.

answer.worked:
Split the integral at the change in the piecewise definition.
$$\begin{align*}\int_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,dx&=1\\\int_{-4}^{0}k(4+x)\,dx+\int_{0}^{4}k(4-x)\,dx&=1\\k\left[4x+\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{-4}^{0}+k\left[4x-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{0}^{4}&=1\\k\big((0+0)-(-16+8)\big)+k\big((16-8)-(0-0)\big)&=1\\8k+8k&=1\\16k&=1\\k&=\frac1{16}.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac1{16}(4+x)&-4\le x\le0,\\\frac1{16}(4-x)&0\le x\le4.\end{cases}$$

spec.description: Unshaded triangular density with labelled intercepts and peak; ordinary source blue marks use house black.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the probability that $0\le X\le2$?

children.label: c
children.prompt: Why is the median zero, and what is the mode?

answer.short: The density is symmetric about $x=0$, with half the probability on either side, so the median is $0$. The mode is $0$.
answer.worked: The density is symmetric about $x=0$, so equal areas lie on either side and $P(X\le0)=\frac12$. Hence the median is $0$. The density has its global maximum at $x=0$, so the mode is $0$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the CDF for $-4\le x\le0$, and the CDF for $0\le x\le4$. Then sketch the whole CDF.

answer.short:
$$F(x)=\begin{cases}\frac{(4+x)^2}{32}&-4\le x\le0,\\1-\frac{(4-x)^2}{32}&0\le x\le4.\end{cases}$$
The curve increases through $(-4,0)$, $(0,\frac12)$ and $(4,1)$, changing from concave up to concave down at $x=0$.
answer.worked:
For $-4\le x\le0$:
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\int_{-4}^{x}\frac1{16}(4+t)\,dt\\&=\frac1{32}\left[(4+t)^2\right]_{-4}^{x}\\&=\frac1{32}\big((4+x)^2-0\big)\\&=\frac{(4+x)^2}{32}.\end{align*}$$
For $0\le x\le4$, note that $F(0)=\frac12$:
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\frac12+\int_0^x\frac1{16}(4-t)\,dt\\&=\frac12-\frac1{32}\left[(4-t)^2\right]_0^x\\&=\frac12-\frac1{32}\big((4-x)^2-16\big)\\&=1-\frac{(4-x)^2}{32}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two equation-driven curved branches with filled endpoints, unlabelled quarter ticks and dashed endpoint guides. Exterior constant branches are not drawn, following the source.
